name: Kayabi
catalog_quote: A sílaba tônica em kaiabi (registrada em negrito) recai na sílaba final da palavra gramatical. Quando há formação de palavra por fixação ou compostção, ocorre a ressilabificação a sílaba tônica passa a ser a última da nova palavra.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim at Souza 2004:33. The classification (fixed final stress on the grammatical word, shifting to new final syllable under suffixation) is stated identically by the primary describer Dobson (2005[1988]:4, 88; 1997:4), files, and independently by Weiss 1998:74 (downloaded now). Nothing found contradicts fixed-strict final. Suggested improvements, not a reclassify: (a) fill the blank grade and cite Dobson 2005[1988]:88 §7 as the primary source, keeping Souza 2004:33 as corroboration (Souza's chapter is a restatement of Dobson 1988); (b) add the secondary-stress rule from Weiss 1998:74 — secondary stress on alternate syllables counting leftward from the final primary; (c) note domain caveats: Weiss frames primary stress as utterance-final before pause, and Dobson 1997 says nominal marker -a and negative/focus -i are unstressed (tup -> túwa; -i for

sources.quote: "The stressed syllable in Kaiabi (marked in bold) falls on the final syllable of the grammatical word. When a word is formed by affixation or compounding, resyllabification occurs and the stressed syllable becomes the last one of the new word."

sources.quote: 'A sílaba tônica com acento mais forte ocorre na última sílaba do enunciado (antes de pausa), e em cada segunda sílaba para a frente do enunciado (em sílabas alternativas), que às vezes resulta numa reestruturação das sílabas: (5.1) /i."pek/ 'pato' (5.2) /'i.pe."ʔyi/ 'pato pequeno' (5.3) /i.'pe.yu."ʔu/ 'pato grande' (5.4) /ja."ʔwat/ 'onça' (5.5) /'ja.ʔwa."run/ 'onça preta'. O ponto /./ simboliza divisão entre sílabas, /"/ representa acentuação forte, e /'/ acento secundário.' Also §5.1.2: CVC only utterance-finally.
sources.note: Independent SIL-fieldworker statement (p. 74) confirming final primary stress and adding alternating secondary stress leftward, which our record's the secondary-stress rule lacks; downloaded now.
